plan.name: plan — best free frontier, degrades to local

observer.description: Frontier observer. Use to decide an approach, review a diff, or resolve an architectural fork — never for bulk edits. Sparse by design: it is the scarce resource.

researcher.description: Answers questions needing current external information via the deep_research pipeline, and writes the report to .agent/research/.

loop.description: Work to completion without handing back
loop.template:
$ARGUMENTS

Work on this autonomously until it is genuinely complete. For this task:

- Do not ask me questions. Where something is ambiguous, make the reasonable
  choice, note it, and keep going.
- Verify your own work as you go — run the tests, run the code, read the output.
  Local tokens are unmetered; spend them on checking rather than on hoping.
- If you get stuck, change approach rather than retrying the same thing.
- Record what you decided with the memory tool as you decide it, not at the end.

When everything is done AND verified, say so plainly and summarise what changed.
If you genuinely cannot finish, say exactly what is blocking you and what you
tried — do not report partial work as complete.

research.description: Deep research: search, read, synthesise, save a cited report
research.template:
Research this thoroughly using the `deep_research` tool:

$ARGUMENTS

Call the tool with a precise, self-contained question — it does not see our
conversation, so put the necessary context into the question itself. When it
returns, give me the answer in your own words: what the evidence actually shows,
where sources disagree, and what remains unknown. Cite the sources it found.

The full report with provenance is saved under `.agent/research/` — tell me the
path. If anything in the answer changes how we should build what we are
building, say so, and record it with the memory tool.

sweep.description: Frontier architecture review of what you just built
sweep.template:
Run a frontier architecture sweep with the `sweep` tool.

$ARGUMENTS

If I did not name files above, sweep the ones you have just been working on.

State the `goal` as THE PROBLEM, not as your solution — the whole value of this
tool is that the frontier model designs independently, without seeing your code,
and a goal phrased as "make the cache use an LRU" leaks the answer and destroys
the comparison. Say "bound memory for a cache with time-varying access
patterns". Pass any real constraints (interfaces you cannot change, dependencies
you cannot add, performance targets) in `constraints`.

When it returns, tell me the verdict and go through the findings. For each one,
say whether you agree — you have read the code and it has not. Then apply what
is worth applying, and record what you deliberately did not apply, and why, with
the memory tool. A finding you rejected for a good reason is worth as much as one
you took.

harness.template:
Work on clank, the harness you are running inside. Its source is at:

    {env:CLANK_HOME}

$ARGUMENTS

Go and look. Use the ordinary tools — `ls`, `grep`, `find`, `cat`, reading files
— to traverse that directory and understand what is actually there before
proposing anything. The parts are: `router/gateway.py` (the model router: route
ladders, the live frontier pool, health, the tool-loop guard, provenance),
`mcp/` (research, memory and sweep servers), `bin/clank` (this CLI),
`opencode.json` (wiring), `PROTOCOL.md` (your own standing instructions),
`DESIGN.md` (why it is shaped this way — read it before changing the shape), and
`logs/calls.jsonl` (every model call ever made, with its full attempt ladder).

That log is evidence. If you want to know whether a route is failing, how often
a rung 429s, or where the time goes, read it rather than speculating.

Two hard rules. Never commit anything that reads more than one credential per
provider — that policy lives in `local/`, which is gitignored and stays that
way. And whatever you change, the local model must remain the last rung of every
ladder: the harness has to keep working with every cloud key revoked.

Verify anything you change against the real router before telling me it works.

remember.description: Record a durable fact about this project
remember.template:
Record this in project memory with the `memory_write` tool:

$ARGUMENTS

Choose the right kind: `fact` for a durable truth (it goes in MEMORY.md and is
loaded into every future session, so keep it to one tight line), `decision` for
an architectural choice — and include what you rejected and why, because that is
the half that saves the next session. Write it so it is useful to someone who
has not read this conversation.

recall.template:
Search project memory with `memory_search` for:

$ARGUMENTS

Then tell me what this project already knows about it — decisions, research,
sweeps, journal. If nothing matches, say so plainly rather than guessing from
the code.

map.description: Rebuild and show the repo symbol map
map.template: Call the `repomap` tool to rebuild the symbol map, then give me a short orientation: what the main pieces are and how they fit together.
